original_question: Let W be a Weyl group of type A and let u <= v in W. Suppose [u,z] is a hypercube decomposition of the Bruhat interval [u,v] in the sense defined in the paper. Does the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) always equal the polynomial P~_{u,v,z}(q) produced from that hypercube decomposition?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.7, which is the paper's exact type-A hypercube-decomposition conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials and explicitly restates the equality P_{u,v}(q)=P~_{u,v,z}(q). ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right target: the type-A setting, a Bruhat interval [u,v], a hypercube decomposition [u,z], the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q), and the conjectural equality with the polynomial P~_{u,v,z}(q) produced from that decomposition. That is exactly the content of Conjecture 1.7. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
missing_details: The paper quantifies over every hypercube decomposition [u,z] of [u,v], not merely over the existence of one chosen decomposition. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should spell out the paper's definition of hypercube decomposition: z < v, [u,z] is diamond complete in [u,v], and for each w in [u,z], the set U(w)={x in [u,v] minus [u,z] : w -> x}, ordered by Bruhat order, spans a hypercube cluster via a unique embedding of the Boolean-lattice digraph P(A) into B(u,v) for every antichain A in U(w). ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

The polynomial P~_{u,v,z}(q) is not arbitrary: the paper says it is computed recursively from the hypercube decomposition [u,z] together with all Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{x,y}(q) for x,y in [u,v] satisfying l(x,y) < l(u,v). ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

The ambient meaning of P_{u,v}(q) should be identified as the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial of W, namely the specialization P^{emptyset,-1}_{u,v}(q)=P^{emptyset,q}_{u,v}(q), which lies in Z[q]. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

If the question is to be fully self-contained, it should also define B(u,v) as the directed graph induced on the interval [u,v] by the Bruhat graph; this notation is used in the hypercube-cluster definition. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
refined_question: Let W be a Weyl group of type A, let u,v in W with u <= v in Bruhat order, and let [u,z] be a hypercube decomposition of the Bruhat interval [u,v], meaning that z < v, [u,z] is diamond complete in [u,v], and for every w in [u,z], the set U(w)={x in [u,v] minus [u,z] : w -> x}, partially ordered by Bruhat order, spans a hypercube cluster in the sense that every antichain A in U(w) admits a unique embedding of directed graphs theta:P(A)->B(u,v) sending the empty set to w and each singleton {a} to a, where P(A) is the Boolean-lattice digraph whose edges correspond to adding one element. If P~_{u,v,z}(q) is the polynomial in Z[q] obtained by the paper's recursive procedure from [u,z] together with all shorter-interval Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{x,y}(q) for x,y in [u,v] with l(x,y) < l(u,v), is it always true that P_{u,v}(q)=P~_{u,v,z}(q) for every such hypercube decomposition [u,z] of [u,v]? ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
justification: Within arXiv:2410.09897, the nearest official formulation is Conjecture 1.7, not the broader combinatorial invariance conjectures. The paper first motivates the search for an explicit Bruhat-interval algorithm, then defines diamond completeness, hypercube clusters, and hypercube decompositions, and finally states exactly the equality P_{u,v}(q)=P~_{u,v,z}(q) for type A. Theorem 1.3 is only needed to make the notation and ambient ring for P_{u,v}(q) precise. The sentence immediately after Conjecture 1.7 records a proved special case from [17, Thm. 3.7], but that special case is not an equivalent reformulation of the conjecture. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))
